extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary institution administrators, Title IX coordinators, campus legal counsel, and other recipients implementing Title IX grievance procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for postsecondary institutions implementing Title IX grievance procedures for complaints of sex-based harassment, including written notice of allegations, timing of meetings, advisor rights, access to evidence, delays for safety, and dismissal/appeal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notice must state presumption of not responsible
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.46(c)(1)(i) requires that the written notice of allegations include a statement that the respondent is presumed not responsible for the alleged conduct until a determination whether sex-based harassment occurred is made at the conclusion of the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must be provided to the parties whose identities are known (respondents and complainants). This presumption supports fairness and reliable outcomes; giving respondents time to prepare for interviews is not unfair or inconsistent with Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to present relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence to decisionmaker(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: The written notice must assure parties that they will have an opportunity to present relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence to trained, impartial decisionmakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient may have more than one decisionmaker; the reference to “a” decisionmaker is not intended to limit that. The limitation to “relevant and not otherwise impermissible” evidence aligns §106.46(c) with §106.46(e)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to access relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence or investigative report
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are “entitled to an equal opportunity to access” the evidence that is relevant to the allegations of sex-based harassment and not otherwise impermissible, and if a postsecondary institution provides access to an investigative report, the parties may request and then must receive access to the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institution has discretion over the mode of providing access (electronic copies, physical copies, or inspection), but must exercise that discretion so parties have an equal opportunity. Access that would conflict with FERPA is addressed by the GEPA override (20 U.S.C. 1221(d)) incorporated at §106.6(e). The Department deleted the word “receive” from one provision to avoid implying a right to keep copies except where specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice may include statement about recipient's prohibition on knowingly making false statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice may alert parties when the recipient's code of conduct has a policy against making false statements in a disciplinary proceeding (final §106.46(c)(1)(iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, §106.45(h)(5) prohibits disciplining a person for making a false statement based solely on the recipient's determination whether sex discrimination occurred; to discipline for a false statement the recipient must find the statement was made knowingly false or in bad faith. The Department removed the phrase “any provision in” to improve flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited delay of notice allowed to address reasonable safety concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.46(c)(3) permits recipients to reasonably delay providing the written notice of allegations to address safety concerns for any person that would arise as a result of providing the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The analysis must be individualized (not based on speculation or stereotypes) and may consider factors such as history of violent/abusive conduct, credible threats of self-harm or harm to others, need for different housing or schedule changes, or substance abuse evidence. Delay should not exceed the time needed to address the safety concern (e.g., allow complainant to relocate) and may not unreasonably delay notice; notice must still be provided with sufficient time for parties to prepare before any initial interview. Recipients must maintain records documenting implementation and the justification for any delay under §106.8(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice must be provided with sufficient time to prepare before initial interview or meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: The first sentence of §106.46(c) requires that the written notice be provided with sufficient time for the parties to prepare a response before any initial interview; §106.46(e)(1) similarly requires sufficient notice of meetings or proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase “with sufficient time for the party to prepare” permits recipient discretion regarding how far in advance notice must be given and applies equally to complainants and respondents. Ensuring sufficient time allows parties to consult advisors, identify witnesses, and prepare, which is important for due process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to provide written notice of additional allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient decides to investigate additional allegations of sex-based harassment by the respondent toward the complainant that were not included in the original notice or were consolidated under §106.45(e), the recipient must provide written notice of those additional allegations to the parties whose identities are known (§106.46(c)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous notice of dismissal generally, with exception if respondent lacked prior notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.46(d) requires notice of dismissal; the Department revised §106.46(d)(1) so that if a dismissal occurs before the respondent has been notified of the allegations, the recipient must provide written notice of the dismissal and the basis for the dismissal only to the complainant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simultaneous notice of dismissal to both parties is appropriate in many cases, but notifying a respondent of a dismissal for which they had no prior notice could cause confusion or risk retaliation; recipients must still comply with §106.45(d)(3) regarding opportunity to appeal dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meetings/proceedings notice applies to participants and must use consistent terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.46(e)(1) requires that recipients give notice of meetings or proceedings to participants “with sufficient time for the party to prepare,” and “participants” refers to those who will be attending the meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to change to “who will be in attendance.” The requirement mirrors Clery Act obligations to provide timely notice of meetings in proceedings based on dating violence, domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to an advisor of choice during any meeting or proceeding in §106.46
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.46(e)(2) requires postsecondary institutions to provide parties the same opportunities to have an advisor of their choice present during any meeting or proceeding as part of the grievance procedures under §106.46.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The advisor may be an attorney. The right applies to postsecondary students and ensures non-student parties in mixed cases have the same opportunity. The institution must permit the advisor's presence in any meeting or proceeding, including investigative interviews. Institutions may establish restrictions on the extent of an advisor's participation, but such restrictions must apply equally to both parties and must not limit the mere presence of the advisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions need not allow multiple advisors; may limit to one advisor of choice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require institutions to allow parties to be accompanied by multiple advisors; §106.46(e)(2) does not require multiple advisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing multiple advisors could cause scheduling delays, chilling effects, and privacy weakening. Students could choose a parent as advisor, but postsecondary students are not given an automatic right for parents to attend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions are not required to pay for parties' legal counsel or advisors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require recipients to pay for parties' legal counsel or advisors because procedural rights afford parties the opportunity to participate regardless of financial ability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, nothing in the regulations prevents an institution from choosing to pay for advisors or to offer attorney-advisors or non-attorney advisors; the status or financial resources of any party must not affect the institution's compliance with equitable treatment and impartial evaluation obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on advisors and role clarity must be applied equally
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may establish restrictions regarding the role an advisor may play in grievance procedures, and any such restrictions must apply equally to the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrictions on advocates are common and necessary for orderly proceedings, but must not disproportionately impair either party. Institutions should provide clarity (in procedures or notice) about the permitted role of advisors and any training or compensation policies, though the Department declined to add additional mandatory specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employees may serve as a party's chosen advisor but institution cannot appoint confidential employees as institution-appointed questioners in live hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may choose a confidential employee to serve as their advisor of choice, but an institution may not appoint or require a confidential employee to serve as the institution's advisor of choice to ask questions on behalf of a party when the party lacks their own advisor; specifically, §106.46(f)(1)(ii)(B) was revised to bar appointing a confidential employee for questioning at live hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves parties' ability to select confidential employees while preventing the institution from delegating questioning duties in a way that implicates confidentiality protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: No categorical prohibition on an advisor serving as a witness; consider witness relationship in credibility assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to require the notice of allegations to specify that a party's advisor may not also serve as a witness. Institutions may establish restrictions regarding an advisor's role, and decisionmakers should consider a witness's relationship to a party when making credibility assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may limit or distinguish roles (e.g., an advisor who is also a witness) but a blanket ban in the regulation was not adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable treatment and impartiality obligations for evidence evaluation and decisionmakers
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must objectively evaluate the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence, treat complainants and respondents equitably, and use investigators and decisionmakers who are free from bias or conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The status of a party's advisor (including whether an advisor is an attorney) and a party's financial resources must not affect the institution's compliance with these obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and recordkeeping of implementation decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.8(f), a recipient must maintain records documenting its implementation of the requirements of §106.46, including the justification for any delay in providing the notice of allegations under §106.46(c)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordkeeping supports review and demonstrates that any delay or safety-based decision was individualized and necessary.
